transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-30
Start time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Anita Rao (Cortexus Head of ML), Markus Vetter (CTO), Sam Casey (Cortexus SE), Lina Ortiz (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Redwood ran an internal enablement with Cortexus team roleplaying objections and clarifying messaging. Focus on quick pitch, demo cadence, and how to frame Dedicated and Private vs Hosted. Security and latency/cost tradeoffs came up; action items assigned.

Topics touched: 2-min pitch, architecture slide walkthrough, KV cache/quantization mention, routing/fallbacks, SSO, audit logs, benchmarking plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: All right thanks everybody for joining, this is the reframe lab. Um the goal today is simple: we want a tight two minute pitch that any AE can use, a demo flow that shows latency/cost tradeoffs and a practiced answer for the dedicated vs hosted question.

[00:27] Priya Desai: Hey everyone, I'll do the technical walk and then we'll break into roleplay. Jordan, do you want to set expectations?

[00:34] Jordan Kim: Yeah, quick. We're going to run the pitch twice, one 'light' pitch for quick inbound and one 'buyer's journey' pitch for mid-market. Then Priya will demo a short request path and we'll rehearse a dedicated/privat rebuttal.

[01:12] Anita Rao: Sounds good. We're playing both the customer and giving feedback, right?

[01:18] Jordan Kim: Exactly. Let's dive. Two minute pitch, take one.

[01:30] Jordan Kim: (pitch) Cortexus, in two minutes: Redwood Inference gives you predictable, production-grade inference so your product teams can ship LLM features without guessing about cost or latency. We provide hosted APIs for fast time-to-value, reserved Dedicated capacity when you need throughput and isolation, and Private VPC/on-prem bundles for regulated data. We optimize at the serving layer — batching, KV cache, quan-tization recommendations — to reduce per-token cost while hitting latency SLOs. So you get consistent performance across environments and a single rollout/ops model.

[02:05] Markus Vetter: Quick interruption — what do you mean by consistent performance across environments?

[02:12] Priya Desai: Good call — we mean the same API and rollout primitives. A model pinned in Hosted behaves the same on Dedicated, and we expose the same tracing and token-level cost metrics in the Console. So feature parity, plus routing and fallbacks if a variant isn't available.

[02:47] Sam Casey: When you say KV cache, can you explain in plain english? Our team sometimes gets fuzzy here.

[02:55] Priya Desai: Sure — think of KV cache as key/value state for the attention cache — we cache previous tokens for repeated prompts or chats to avoid recomputing. It reduces tokens and compute for follow-on requests, so p95 drops. Apologies if that's a bit jargon-y in a quick pitch.

[03:30] Jordan Kim: Ok roleplay time — Anita you pretend to be a skeptical procurement lead, Markus is CTO. Priya and I will try the workshop pitch.

[03:45] Anita Rao: (role) We have concerns about vendor lock and data residency. How are you different from the big clouds.

[03:55] Jordan Kim: Short answer: we provide a migration path and exportable models. More importantly, unlike some managed clouds that treat inference as a black box, Redwood gives you perf visibility, routing policies and the option for Private deployment with audit logs and KMS integration so you control keys.

[04:30] Markus Vetter: We're regulated — we need SOC 2, SSO, and HSM-backed keys. Can you support that?

[04:38] Priya Desai: Yes — we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, tenant-level audit logs and KMS/HSM integrations in Private. We also offer an optional on-prem package if you need air-gapped installs. We'll share our security packet.

[05:05] Jordan Kim: (note) action: send SOC 2 docs; share KMS integration doc.

[05:30] Sam Casey: Objection — what about latency? Our product needs p95 under 350ms for 512 tokens and we do a lot of short queries.

[05:40] Priya Desai: Depending on model and model variant we can tune for latency with smaller sequence-optimized variants, continuous batching settings and inference kernels. For short queries we recommend smaller decoder models or quantized variants on Dedicated or colocated hosts. We'll propose a benchmark plan.

[06:20] Jordan Kim: Let's shift to the demo flow. Priya, walk the request path and the Console screens you'd show in a 6-7 minute demo.

[06:30] Priya Desai: High level: call the API -> model catalog selection -> runtime routing -> trace and token cost view -> rollout config. I'll show a quick trace from the Console: request shows 120ms model time, 30ms routing, token-level cost and per-route breakdown. If we switch to Dedicated, throughput scales but we keep the same API endpoint.

[07:05] Anita Rao: Can you flip to the trace where a fallback happens? We want to see graceful degradation.

[07:12] Priya Desai: Yep — here you can see automatic fallback to a slightly smaller model with a note in the trace and an alert. It's not perfect word-for-word but it preserves a good quality level and keeps SLAs.

[07:50] Jordan Kim: Good. Now objections practice: "Why not just use OpenAI?" Priya, your rebuttal.

[07:58] Priya Desai: Reframe: If your needs are pure upstream model quality and you want the fastest time-to-market, sure; but if you care about production economics, auditability and multi-environment parity, Redwood reduces ops overhead and cost. We also give you model variant management and quantization recommendations that directly lower per-token spend.

[08:40] Markus Vetter: What about competition from Anthropic or self-hosting with Replicate?

[08:48] Jordan Kim: For Anthropic — similar capability but different pricing/licensing and less focus on dedicated production runtime. For Replicate/self-hosting — you get control but you also carry the full ops burden: tuning kernels, autoscaling, KV cache, and building rollout tooling. Redwood packages that work out of the box.

[09:20] Anita Rao: Ok structure feedback — the pitch is good but it feels overloaded. Recommend two short soundbites: one for the executive, one for the infra lead.

[09:30] Jordan Kim: Good feedback. We'll codify: Exec pitch = "Predictable inference economics and consistent performance across environments." Infra pitch = "A production-first serving runtime with auditability, routing, and private deployment options so you don't build ops yourself."

[10:05] Jordan Kim: Let's rehearse the demo cold-open. Priya you open with the one-liner, then show Console, then show the perf table.

[10:20] Priya Desai: (demo) One-liner: Redwood gives predictable inference so your teams ship features faster without guessing about latency or runaway cost. Quick Console: model catalog, trace, per-token cost, rollout. Table: p50/p95 latency with hosted vs dedicated.

[11:00] Sam Casey: Minor nit — can we have a slide that maps customer workloads to recommended model family and quantization profile? That would help our engineering reviewers.

[11:10] Priya Desai: Yes that's in the Optimize toolkit; I'll extract a simple mapping: chat-heavy -> medium decoder with KV cache enabled; short completions -> smaller decoder quantized; high-throughput -> Dedicated with burst capacity.

[11:50] Jordan Kim: Roleplay variant: now Anita as procurement pushes on price. Priya, handle price objection.

[11:59] Priya Desai: We lead with unit economics — show per-token cost before and after caching and batching. Then propose a Dedicated tier for predictability and a pilot with a crediting model so you can validate unit economics.

[12:35] Anita Rao: Would need a clear exit — if we don't see cost improvements we need to avoid long lock-in.

[12:40] Jordan Kim: We'll include an exit clause in the pilot and a migration checklist; action item noted.

[13:05] Lina Ortiz: Quick ask — can you show how rollouts and canaries work? We want to do canary for model versioning.

[13:12] Priya Desai: Sure — show the Routes page: you can set traffic splits by percentage, perform canary rollouts, and configure automatic fallback to earlier model variants if evaluation metrics drop. All observable in Console and tie to eval sets.

[13:50] Jordan Kim: Bringing this back: agreed canonical two-minute pitch and a trimmed demo clip for AE training. Priya will build a mini-benchmark script and Jordan will share pricing and security pack.

[14:10] Anita Rao: We'll send a sample dataset and our p95 objective.

[14:20] Sam Casey: One more technical nit — how do you handle KV cache eviction on long multi-turn chats?

[14:28] Priya Desai: We have LRU-ish eviction policies and you can configure prefix caching TTLs. Also note that for very long histories we recommend summarization or windowing to keep token counts down.

[15:00] Jordan Kim: Great. Any other hot takes?

[15:05] Markus Vetter: The pitch feels good after the trim. Try to be less product-surge and more outcome-surge: "We cut p95 by X and reduce unit cost by Y" — add concrete numbers if possible.

[15:25] Jordan Kim: Noted — action for Priya to run the benchmark and return numbers.

[15:40] End of roleplay. Quick recap and next steps.

[15:45] Jordan Kim: Recap: finalize 2-min pitch, make AE training clip, run benchmark, send security docs and sample pricing. We'll reconvene after the pilot scoping is ready. Thanks everyone.

[16:00] Meeting ends (short recording for enablement purposes).

Notes on transcript quality: auto-generated, occasional mis-heard words (e.g., quan-tization spelled weird, K-V cash for KV cache), speaker attribution mostly correct but could be slightly off.
